forbidden.name: api-contracts-is-a-leaf
forbidden.comment: src/api/contracts.ts is imported by the browser bundle. It may only depend on the catalog type vocabulary; anything else would drag server code toward frontend/ and make the contract depend on the persistence it exists to decouple from.

forbidden.name: frontend-reaches-server-only-through-contracts
forbidden.comment: The browser bundle may share the HTTP contracts and nothing else. Importing a repository, the router or crawler code would either break the bundle or ship server logic to users.

forbidden.name: server-does-not-import-frontend
forbidden.comment: frontend/ is a browser bundle entry, never a library for the Worker.

forbidden.name: catalog-does-not-depend-on-persistence
forbidden.comment: The catalog domain — categories, manufacturers, identity, knowledge verification — decides meaning, not storage. It must stay testable without a database, so mapping goes db -> catalog and never back.

forbidden.name: repositories-do-not-depend-on-orchestration
forbidden.comment: Repositories are called by the crawler and the HTTP layer; depending back on either would make persistence unusable from a different entrypoint and invite cycles.

forbidden.name: crawler-does-not-know-about-catalog-verification
forbidden.comment: The crawler collects listings; Knowledge Catalog verification is a separate pipeline that later reads what the crawler stored. They meet through the database, not through each other's types — which is what a verification queue message type sitting in the crawler vocabulary had quietly undone.

forbidden.name: knowledge-catalog-does-not-borrow-crawler-env-types
forbidden.comment: Knowledge verification and its queue own their configuration contracts. They may reuse crawler infrastructure such as robots-respecting fetch, but must not depend on CrawlerEnv just to read deployment settings.

forbidden.name: queue-policy-stays-pure
forbidden.comment: src/knowledge-catalog/policy.ts holds the retry, lease and promotion decisions so they can be read and tested without a database, a queue or the network. Type-only imports are fine; a value import from a repository or the verifier would put I/O back inside the policy and make those rules untestable again.

forbidden.name: manufacturer-strategies-are-composed-only-by-the-verifier
forbidden.comment: Manufacturer-specific verification behavior is wired in at src/catalog/knowledge-verification/verifier.ts. If a generic strategy or the shared page verifier imported one, per-manufacturer conditionals would be back inside the code that must stay manufacturer-agnostic.

forbidden.name: shop-adapters-are-reached-through-the-registry
forbidden.comment: Generic code composes shops through src/crawler/shops/index.ts. Importing a concrete adapter — or the registration machinery in registry.ts — directly is how shop-specific branches get back into shared code.

forbidden.name: shops-do-not-reach-persistence-or-the-api
forbidden.comment: A shop reports seller facts. Persistence, search projection, evidence retention and HTTP behavior are platform stages that run after it, and a shop that could call them directly would be able to bypass one. The only exception is the activity-policy vocabulary, which the composition root reads to attach a shop's user-facing update semantics.

forbidden.name: product-search-sql-stays-a-vocabulary
forbidden.comment: src/db/product-search-entity-sql.ts is the one definition of what a search entity is, shared by the incremental sync, the deterministic rebuild and the migration backfill. It must stay pure SQL text with no dependencies: the moment it can reach a repository or the catalog, the three callers can start disagreeing about grouping again.

forbidden.name: domain-code-does-not-import-shops
forbidden.comment: The catalog domain and the repositories are what shops feed, never the other way round. Reaching the registry from either would make canonical catalog decisions depend on which shops happen to be registered.
